newsitem.title: USA: NYPA shuts 832 MW Fitzpatrick plant for repairs.
newsitem.headline: NYPA shuts 832 MW Fitzpatrick plant for repairs.

text.p: The New York Power Authority (NYPA) said Friday it shut its 832 megawatt (MW) Fitzpatrick nuclear plant to remove fish and debris accumulated on screens in water intakes that supply cooling water to the plant.
"The plant is expected to return to service early next week," NYPA said in a statement.

NYPA said it shut the Scriba, N.Y., generating station to prevent damage to the screens. Earlier, operators reduced the plant's power output to 57 percent to slow down the rate of accumulations on the screens.
Water from the intakes cools the plant's condenser and is returned to Lake Ontario. The condenser cools steam, which has been used to power the plant's turbine.
The other NYPA nuclear power plant, the 965 MW Indian Point 3 along the Hudson River, remained shut after it was taken off line last Saturday to repair its feedwater heaters.
NYPA produces about a fourth of New York state's electricity
